scope: For the 3-head chart and fixed 4x5 grid state R in frontier-20261028-grid-phase-interpolation-v1.json SHA256 e1f92daf6dca9ae2a2196bc205ee48c690531ae654a8d4614774dbd185e4dd1e, this exactly optimizes its family H_p>=0 over the mixing parameter p. It is a sufficient SN<=2 condition for those projections, NOT a necessary condition for Schmidt number and NOT a universal theorem.
starting_identity: The cited written identity gives an actual SR2 decomposition whenever H_p=diag(3,3-pT,3-(1-p)T)-t*t^*>=0 for some p in [0,1], where T=|v1|^2 and t=(1,-v0,-v2). This identity is the convex combination of the exact 5-phase and 4-phase rank2 seeds, their leftover (1-p)[D'] and a 3x3 Gram over vectors supported on Alice rows2,3.
optimal_criterion: Write a=|v0|, b=|v2|. If T>6 no H_p is PSD because its last two diagonal budgets sum to 6-T<0. At T=6, H_p is PSD exactly when a=b=0 and p=1/2. For 0<T<6 let S=6-T, ell=max(0,3-T), u=min(3,S). Feasible x=3-pT and y=3-(1-p)T obey x in [ell,u], y=S-x, and x,y>=0. If a+b=0, H_p is PSD for every choice of feasible x. Otherwise define x*=clip(S*a/(a+b),ell,u), y*=S-x*. With convention 0/0=0 and positive numerator/0=+infinity, there exists p with H_p>=0 iff 1/3+a^2/x*+b^2/y*<=1. For T=0 the criterion is a^2+b^2<=2.
proof: For nonzero denominators, the matrix determinant lemma/rank-one Schur complement gives H_p>=0 iff 1/3+a^2/x+b^2/y<=1. If a denominator vanishes, positive semidefiniteness forces the corresponding numerator to vanish and the same condition applies after dropping that coordinate. The function f(x)=a^2/x+b^2/(S-x) is convex on its positive interval; f'(x)=0 exactly at x=S*a/(a+b) (for positive a,b). Clipping to the feasible interval is the global minimum; the one-zero cases follow by monotonicity and the stated 0/0 convention. Conversely any feasible x is attained by p=(3-x)/T. The T=6 and T=0 endpoints are direct.
clean_large_middle_region: For 3<=T<6, S<=3, so the unconstrained optimum is always feasible: x*=S*a/(a+b), y*=S*b/(a+b), including a=0 or b=0 by continuity. Cauchy-Schwarz gives f_min=(a+b)^2/S. Thus every chart point with 3<=|v1|^2<6 and (|v0|+|v2|)^2 <= (2/3)(6-|v1|^2) has SN<=2. This strictly contains the previous p=1/2 region whenever the head amplitudes are unequal.
explicit_four_support_point: At v=(1,2,1/10), T=4,a=1,b=1/10, the optimal x=20/11,y=2/11 corresponds to p=13/44. The Schur sum is 563/600<1; exact H pivots are [2,7/22,37/385]. It is outside the preceding half-half quadratic region because 4+3(1+1/100)=703/100>6, and both endpoint Grams are invalid since T=4>3. The kernel |3>-|0>-2|1>-(1/10)|2> has four nonzero coordinates. The projected state is PPT with SN<=2; no entanglement claim is made.

exact_check.observed: The checker hash-pins and replays all three cases in the preceding phase checker, then checks the p=13/44 example by all five-phase rank-minor polynomials, all four individual four-phase rank minors, all 256 state entries, Fraction/Gaussian rational Gram pivots and the actual partial-transpose pivots. The resulting Schur sum is exactly 563/600. The all-complex optimum is justified by the written convex minimization rather than the finite check.

limits: Only mixtures of the two displayed phase seeds are optimized; more SR2 decompositions could exist outside this region. The reflected |4>-tail chart follows from the previously certified local symmetry, and generic nonzero |3>,|4> kernels and unrestricted 4x4 PPT states remain open. No independent review, formal proof, or novelty claim.
